messages:
alex: quick triage — seeing ~12% p95 regression on Mixtral-8B when using the fp8 KV-cache path since the kernel-router change earlier today. profiler hints attached, anyone oncall?

mike: on it. which workload did you run? long context or short chatgen?

alex: long-history completions, seq_len ~1024, prefix cache hit ~40%. regression spikes line up with compaction events.

jess: saw something related on Qwen when we bumped RoPE scaling last week. my suspicion: prefetch offsets + slab compaction are producing unaligned pointers that force fallback kernels.

perf-bot: profiler snapshot (condensed):
  kernel_router.cpp:234 select_kernel() -> chose generic_gemm fallback
  kernel_latency: generic_gemm 6.2ms vs optimized_fp8_gemm 2.1ms
  kv_compaction: pause 1.8ms (bounce buffer + quant step)

ryan: do we have the router rules? if it prefers fp8 but alignment doesn't match, fallback is expected.

alex: router snippet (current canary):
```
kernel_router:
  prefer_fp8: true
  align_bytes: 64
  min_head_dim_for_fp8: 32
  fallback_threshold_ms: 0.5
```

mike: Mixtral-8B head_dim=40 and kv_dim=320. with our allocator returning pages that sometimes start at 32-byte offsets, 64-byte alignment requirement fails. changing align_bytes to 32 for that model should avoid the fallback.

jess: extra detail: during compaction we allocate a temporary bounce buffer in fp16, copy then quantize back to fp8. that copy creates a different pointer alignment and the kernel router sees non-64-aligned ptr and chooses generic path. the quant step costs ~1.2ms and also flips the kernel decision.

emily: ran a canary experiment: set align_bytes=32 & disable bounce-quant during compaction for the Mixtral pool. results: p95 down ~7% (110ms -> 102ms), throughput +3%, no OOMs. accuracy short-checks look fine.

mike: suggested quick-fix config for mixtral pool: 
```
models:
  mixtral-8b:
    kernel_router:
      align_bytes: 32
      prefer_fp8: true
    kv_cache:
      compaction:
        use_bounce_quant: false
        eviction_batch: 16
```

ryan: i'll add allocator guard in a PR so allocations for fp8 kernels are 64-byte aligned when required. long-term we should avoid changing router align heuristics per-model, but this is a pragmatic stopgap. i'll also add an assertion in unit tests that kernel selection is stable across compaction.

infra-bot: deploying canary: align_bytes=32 -> cluster:dedicated-mixtral-pool-3, windows: 2h, route: 5% traffic. (deployment id: deploy_2026_03_18_42)

perf-bot: canary metrics (60m): p95 latency 110ms -> 102ms, cpu tail jitter -15%, kv_compaction_avg 1.9ms -> 1.1ms. no increased allocation churn detected.

alex: great. follow-ups: 1) PR for allocator alignment (ryan), 2) disable bounce-quant feature flag default false for mixtral until we have aligned allocator (mike/emily), 3) add compaction-bounce-duration telemetry and a regression alert (jess). i'll file tickets.

jess: also flag: RoPE scaling interaction — we precompute sin/cos in fp16 and store in KV (to save memory) and then quantize for fp8 cache. small numeric drift when rope_scale != 1 observed in evals. add a regression test for rope_scale != 1 + fp8 quant.

alex: noted. thanks all :thumbsup: 

mike: tagging @ryan for the allocator PR and @infra-bot for canary watch.

ryan: picking this up now, will push small allocator patch and tests by EOD.

emily: will collect perf traces for the next 24h and post flamegraphs if anything else pops.

alex: perfect. we'll regroup after the canary completes.
